research_question: Can learned use of positive and confusion-region corrections transfer a visual distinction to independent environments with fewer verified corrections, while retaining independently useful OlmoEarth representations?

core_datasets.name: PASTIS/PASTIS-R
core_datasets.role: crop-confusion region transfer using dense parcel/crop labels and satellite time series

core_datasets.name: Kuro Siwo
core_datasets.role: flood versus permanent-water confusion and event transfer with two pre-event and one post-event SAR observations
unresolved: sigma0 to native S1 preprocessing contract

extension_dataset.name: MADOS
extension_dataset.role: marine debris versus visually similar materials
constraints: sparse unlabeled pixels are not negatives
Rayleigh-corrected reflectance differs from S2 L2A
no individual-item mass or long-term increase ground truth

architecture_candidate: jointly train OlmoEarth while preserving dense spatial-temporal feature grid
encode positive and verified confusion regions with the same encoder
condition region/observation selection on correction distinction and provenance-controlled environment metadata
share dense prediction head with strong generic baselines
provide bounded evidence tokens and source identifiers to the actual VLM

learning_candidate.optional_utility: support-induced loss change estimated only in training data with geography/year/parent cross-fitting

supervision: same added utility or paired supervision

extra: specialist segmentation plus exact operators plus same VLM
identical cached dense outputs supplied to different readers
encoder-only and fixed independent EO evaluation

evaluation.primary_units: independent parent geographies/events; do not count pixels or derived questions as independent replications
evaluation.primary_goal: corrected distinction transfer at equal total expert-label cost
metrics: corrections required to reach a prespecified quality level
evaluation.no_correction_control: only for readers with a defined no-support path; no undefined K=0 prototype
controls: same dense outputs to both readers
